keyVerseText: Of Simeon; Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.
rootMeaning: The root of צוּרִישַׁדַּי (Zurishaddai) combines צוּר (tsûwr), meaning 'rock' or 'cliff,' with שַׁדַּי (Shadday), meaning 'Almighty.' This compound literally conveys 'my rock is Almighty' or 'rock of the Almighty.' The imagery of a rock here is not merely a physical stone but a symbol of strength, refuge, and divine protection, emphasizing God's unshakable power and reliability beyond the common English gloss of a simple name.
usageInScripture: The name Zurishaddai appears five times in Scripture, consistently translated as 'of Zurishaddai,' indicating a proper name rather than a descriptive title. All occurrences relate to a Simeonite individual, specifically the father of Shelumiel, a tribal leader during the exodus. This consistent usage as a personal name highlights the integration of divine attributes into Israelite identity and heritage.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding Zurishaddai as 'my rock is Almighty' enriches our grasp of how God’s strength and sovereignty were personally embraced by His people, even in their names. It reflects a foundational truth in Scripture: God is the unmovable rock and almighty protector of His covenant community. This name points believers to the steadfastness of God, who is both a refuge and a powerful defender, a truth ultimately fulfilled in Christ, the cornerstone of our faith. Recognizing the divine element in Zurishaddai invites reflection on God's enduring presence and power in the lives of His people.
keyVerseReflection: Numbers 1:6 states, 'Of Simeon; Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.' Here, Zurishaddai functions as a patriarchal identifier, linking Shelumiel to a lineage whose name declares trust in God’s almighty strength. The presence of this name in the census underscores the importance of divine strength as foundational to Israel’s tribal leadership and identity during the wilderness journey.
